---
title: "CI & Release"
---

Every artifact is built by Nix from one lockfile: CI and a local machine produce
byte-identical images from the same derivations. No `docker build` and no
Dockerfile exists in the build path.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    trig["v* tag, or workflow_dispatch"] --> build["build-images<br/>nix build .#image-&lt;svc&gt; (matrix x4)"]
    build --> smoke{"smoke-stack<br/>compose up --wait from fresh images<br/>INSTREAM probes + decision-log assertions"}
    smoke -- "pass, tag ref" --> pub["publish-images<br/>GHCR :latest + :version + SPDX SBOM"]
    smoke -- "pass, dispatch" --> rehearse["stop: rehearsal only,<br/>nothing published"]
    smoke -- "fail" --> dump["failure dump:<br/>compose logs + docker inspect states"]
    pub --> notes["draft release:<br/>digests, changelog, SBOM assets"]
```

## Workflows

| Workflow | Triggers | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `flake-check.yml` | PRs, pushes to `master` | `nix flake check --all-systems --no-build` + image-closure dry-run builds |
| `release-images.yml` | tags `v*`, `workflow_dispatch` | build → smoke gate → publish → draft release (publish and release require a tag ref) |
| `tests.yml` | tags `v*`, `workflow_dispatch` | addon unit suite (`pytest tests/`, mitmproxy stubbed) |

Merge-path CI is deliberately light: flake-check, pre-commit.ci, and
dependency-review only. The heavy jobs (image builds, compose smoke, unit
suite) run on the release path — tags and manual dispatch — so merges stay fast.

## The smoke gate

`smoke-stack` is the release-quality gate: a full compose deployment from the
**freshly built images** (never from GHCR), exercising the verdict path
end-to-end before anything can be published.

1. Images are loaded into the runner's daemon from the build job's artifacts.
2. `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f tests/smoke-override.yml up -d --wait`
   brings up the stack: local image refs, published probe ports, dnsmasq
   upstream servers, and a stubbed openvpn (the smoke verifies images and the
   verdict path; tunnel verification needs real PKI and runs in the
   [verdict test suite](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/15)).
3. `tests/instream_probe.py` waits for clamd (`--wait`, polling a clean probe),
   then asserts both verdicts over the INSTREAM protocol: benign bytes →
   `CLEAN`, [EICAR](https://www.eicar.org/download-anti-malware-testfile/) →
   `INFECTED`.
4. Decision-log assertions: requests through the explicit proxy
   (`example.com` passlisted → `splice`, `wikipedia.org` unlisted → `bump`)
   must appear with those verdicts in `decisions.jsonl`.

A failure at any step blocks `publish-images` — nothing broken reaches GHCR.
The failure dump captures compose logs plus `docker inspect` runtime state
(exit code, error, OOM) for every container.

## Rehearsals vs releases

`workflow_dispatch` runs the identical build + smoke pipeline without a tag;
`publish-images` and `release-notes` require `refs/tags/v*` and are skipped
 otherwise. Dispatches are therefore full **rehearsals** with zero registry
side effects.

The gate earned its place in six consecutive rehearsals — each caught a real
image/addon runtime defect that build-time checks cannot see:

| Rehearsal | Defect caught | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | dnsmasq: no `/etc/passwd` in image → privilege-drop fails (exit 1) | [#43](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/43) | #36 |
| #2 | dnsmasq: no `/etc/group`, `/var/run` → pidfile failure (exit 3) | [#44](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/44) | #37 |
| #3 | clamav entry: `install` not in image PATH; no shell binary (silent exit 1) | [#45](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/45) | #40 |
| #4 | freshclam: no `DatabaseMirror` → no DB → clamd fails dead | [#46](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/46) | #42 |
| #4+ | addon: `CLAMD_ADDR` hardcoded loopback vs compose `CLAMD_HOST=clamav` → scan fail-open | [#47](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/47) | #32 |
| #5 | `/var/lib/clamav` not writable by uid 900 → DB bootstrap fails | [#48](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/issues/48) | #49 |
| #6 | — | — | **PASS** ([run](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/actions/runs/36806070984)) |

Rehearsal #6 cleared all assertions: build ×4, `CLEAN`/`INFECTED` INSTREAM
probes, and the `splice`/`bump` decision-log lines through real proxy traffic.
The defect ledger (#43–#48) documents each finding with symptom, root cause,
and the verifying run.

## Images

Built with `pkgs.dockerTools.buildLayeredImage` from
[`nix/images.nix`](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/blob/master/nix/images.nix);
image entrypoints reference every binary by absolute store path (no PATH
resolution inside images) and bake the minimal `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/group`,
and runtime directories each service requires. Outputs are Linux-only; darwin
systems skip image outputs.

```bash
nix run .#load-images     # build all four locally + docker load (linux host)
```

## Publishing a release

Releases are **GPG-signed tags**; the release job verifies the signature
(`git tag -v`) and aborts on an unsigned or badly signed tag:

```bash
VERSION=v0.1.1   # example

git tag -s $VERSION -m "OpenSASE $VERSION: release summary"
git push origin $VERSION
```

The pipeline then builds, smoke-tests, and publishes all four images to GHCR
(`:latest` + the version), and opens a **draft release** generated on the
runner:

- digest table for all four images (with a note that the images passed the smoke gate)
- commit changelog since the previous tag
- SPDX SBOMs attached as release assets
- 60-second compose deploy snippet

Publish the draft to ship; consumers need only an OCI runtime. Kubernetes
consumers apply [`k8s/manifests.yaml`](https://github.com/shsingh/opensase/blob/master/k8s/manifests.yaml),
rendered from `k8s/manifests.cue` (`nix run .#k8s-manifests`).

## Docs site

`pages.yml` renders this site with Quarto and deploys to GitHub Pages on
pushes to `master` that touch `_quarto.yml`, `docs/**`, `index.qmd`, or the
README.
